issue: Does the physical restraint enhancement under U.S.S.G. § 2B3.1(b)(4)(B) require that the restraint be sustained, with a focus on the victim for more than a brief moment, or can a brief restraint suffice?

sides.position: The restraint must be sustained, with a focus on the victim for a meaningful duration; a few seconds of restraint is not enough (the narrow view).
cases: United States v. Bell, No. 17-3792 (3d Cir. 2020)

sides.position: A brief restraint can satisfy the physical restraint enhancement, even if it lasts only moments (the broader "sustained focus" standard applied in Coleman).
cases: United States v. Coleman, 664 F.3d 1047 (6th Cir. 2012)

this_court: adopts the narrow Ninth Circuit view on duration (majority adopts the narrow view and finds no sustained focus on the victim); the dissent disagrees on application to these facts
quote: Although I refrain from commenting on the propriety of adopting this factor — that is, whether the majority was correct to adopt the narrow view of the Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit in the circuit split on this issue — I believe that Bell’s conduct also satisfies this factor.
cite: United States v. Marquise Bell, No. 17-3792 (3rd Cir. 2020)
